title: Fence appeal approved, Humane Society funding, Moore Avenue tender
subtitle: Housing Accelerator Fund launch, trail and bikeway funding, police update, and climate and asset management presentation
overview: Council approved an appeal of a fence variance for a corner property on Wasaga Crescent, overturning the Committee of Adjustment's denial of an 8-foot fence in the flankage yard {{vote:m7}}. Approval carries conditions: the applicant pays the City's legal costs and provides a survey confirming the fence sits entirely on private property.

Council also committed $200,000 over three years to the Humane Society's new building {{vote:m10}}, released $570,000 for trail and bikeway work with a $306,000 transfer to the Hydro Corridor project {{vote:m11}}, and awarded the Moore Avenue South reconstruction tender for $2,944,820.64 {{vote:m12}}. Traffic and parking by-law amendments passed on consent {{vote:m8}}.

Council received staff's report launching the Housing Accelerator Fund initiatives {{vote:m9}}. Residents can follow progress through project pages on Engage Waterloo. Council also heard updates from the regional police chief and from staff on climate change and asset management. A public meeting on 249-253 Sunview Street was deferred to a later date. The meeting followed a closed session, and the minutes record no public decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved the appeal of the fence variance application, subject to the applicant covering the City's legal costs and confirming by survey that the fence is entirely on private property.
Council approved $200,000 for the Humane Society's new building, paid over three years at $66,667 per year from the Community Priority and Contingency Reserve.
Council released $570,000 of 2024 capital funding for Trail & Bikeway Master Plan implementation and transferred $306,000 to the Hydro Corridor project.
Council awarded RFT24-09 for road reconstruction from John Street to Erb Street to Network Sewer and Watermain Ltd. for a total of $2,944,820.64.
Council approved the amendments to Traffic and Parking By-law 08-077 at various locations, passed on the consent agenda.
Council received the report launching the City's eight federally funded Housing Accelerator Fund initiatives, for information.

debate: On the fence appeal, the appellant questioned why the City offers a variance process if the six-foot limit must be obeyed, and said the contractor chose the height without discussing by-laws. Staff said variances can be approved, often with design changes like lattice or landscaping.

Councillors differed on the fence. One favoured upholding the committee's denial, citing no substantive reason such as a safety issue. Another saw the fence as reasonable for the neighbourhood and said the appeal was far cheaper than rebuilding. Staff noted the fence appears to sit in an easement and its exact location was not confirmed.

On the Housing Accelerator Fund, councillors asked about leasing versus selling municipal land, and about the acquisition program for not-for-profits. One councillor asked for options and information from other cities on reducing parking minimums in the Official Plan review. Staff said zero minimums would be hard because developers report condos are difficult to sell without parking.

In the police update, councillors asked about reducing reliance on 911, and about how uniformed officers at community events affect some residents. One councillor raised concern that media releases describing offenders as youth could further criminalize marginalized youth. The chief said police were highlighting that organized crime was using young people.

On the Humane Society request, councillors asked why it missed the budget cycle and how the amount was set. Staff said the timing did not align. The Humane Society said it was based on talks with other humane societies. One councillor was disappointed the region did not fund it.
